title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical People Operations guide for hiring, onboarding, and the performance & feedback cycle at Redwood Inference. It is intended for hiring managers, people managers, interviewers, and new hires. It consolidates process steps, responsibilities, templates, and operational SLAs so teams can run consistent, compliant, and scalable people processes.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Intro: Our hiring process balances speed and quality while ensuring fairness, diversity, and compliance. Below is the standard workflow used for all non-executive technical and product roles. Exceptions (e.g., executive hires, acquisitions) follow the Exec Hiring Addendum (link in related pages).

High-level steps:
- Requisition and role definition (hiring manager + people-ops)
- Sourcing and outreach (recruiting)
- Recruiter screen (30 min)
- Technical/functional interviews (2–3 loops depending on level)
- Hiring manager interview & fit conversation
- Take-home or work sample (optional; role-specific)
- Final interview (leadership/peer panel where applicable)
- Calibration and debrief (panel consensus, rubric review)
- Offer and negotiation (people-ops + hiring manager)
- Pre-onboarding (paperwork, equipment, first-week scheduling)

Responsibilities and SLAs:
- Hiring manager: own job spec, interviewers, and final hiring decision recommendation (SLA: create requisition within 5 business days of approval).
- Recruiter: candidate outreach and scheduling (SLA: initial outreach within 3 business days of open role).
- Interviewers: complete interviewer training module before participating and submit feedback within 48 hours of interview.
- People-ops: coordinate offers, compensation calibration, and background checks; finalize offer letters within 2 business days of approval.

Interview structure and rubrics:
- Use the standardized interview rubric (section below). Each interviewer rates: Role Competence, Problem Solving, Communication, Collaboration, and Culture Add. Ratings: 1 (does not meet) – 5 (exceeds).
- Minimum hire threshold: average >= 3.5 with no single category below 3.
- Disqualifying criteria must be documented in the feedback form with concrete examples.

Interview rubric (table)
| Category | Definition | Rating Guidance |
|---|---:|---|
| Role Competence | Depth of technical/product skills required for the role | 1–5 with examples (code samples, system design notes) |
| Problem Solving | Approach to open problems, tradeoffs, and debugging | Look for structured decomposition and clarity |
| Communication | Explains reasoning clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders | Clear, concise, active listening |
| Collaboration | Track record of working with cross-functional teams | Examples of partnering and resolving conflict |
| Culture Add | Alignment to company values and mission | Evidence of curiosity, ownership, and empathy |

Diversity & compliance notes:
- Use standardized job descriptions and inclusive language checklist.
- Diverse interview panels encouraged for mid+ roles.
- All offer negotiations must be reported to people-ops for pay equity review.
- Maintain candidate data retention per Data Retention Policy (90 days for pipeline, longer for closed loops when required)

2) New hire onboarding (first 90 days)

Goal: Enable new employees to contribute confidently and build relationships. Onboarding is owned by the hiring manager with people-ops and IT support.

Pre-boarding (before day 1):
- Offer accepted → people-ops triggers background check and sends welcome packet in 24 hours.
- IT: provision laptop, accounts (email, Slack, internal tools), and access to basic repos within 3 business days.
- Manager: share first-week schedule, reading list, team org chart, and mentor/ buddy assignment prior to start.

Day 1–7: orientation and role ramp
- Day 1: HR orientation (benefits, payroll, policies), security briefing, team lunch (virtual or in-person).
- Week 1: role onboarding, review of codebase/ product epic, meet key stakeholders, set initial 30/60/90 goals.

30/60/90 day plan (template)
- 30 days: complete core onboarding, contribute to small bug/feature, finish mandatory trainings.
- 60 days: own a medium-scope task with mentorship, lead a retro or onboarding artifact.
- 90 days: independently deliver a measurable outcome aligned to team goals and get manager’s recommendation for full ramp.

Onboarding checklist (sample)
1. Complete HR paperwork and benefits enrollment (people-ops)
2. Receive and test laptop and credentials (IT)
3. Attend security and privacy training (security)
4. Complete codebase walkthrough and local dev environment setup (engineering mentor)
5. Schedule 1:1s with manager and cross-functional partners (manager)
6. Deliver first-week progress update in #new-hires channel (new hire)

Continuing support:
- Assigned buddy for first 90 days.
- Manager weekly 1:1s for first 60 days, then cadence as standard.
- People-ops check-ins at 30 and 90 days for onboarding feedback and program improvement.

3) Performance & feedback cycle

Overview: Redwood uses a continuous feedback culture paired with a formal quarterly review cycle. Managers provide ongoing coaching; formal reviews consist of a self-assessment, peer feedback, manager assessment, and calibration.

Cadence and timeline:
- Ongoing: weekly 1:1s, monthly team check-ins, and real-time feedback.
- Quarterly: self-assessment submitted (deadline: last business day of quarter), peer feedback collected (automated survey), manager review completed (within 10 business days after quarter close).
- Calibration: leadership and people-ops run a calibration meeting to ensure role-level consistency and pay decisions (within 3 weeks of quarter close).

Review components:
- Self-assessment: achievements, challenges, goals for next quarter, and examples supporting competency ratings.
- Peer feedback: 4–8 peers recommended by manager; anonymized summary provided to reviewer.
- Manager assessment: competency ratings (1–5), goal progress, impact examples, development plan, and compensation recommendation if applicable.

Rating scales and decision rules:
- Competencies (core): Ownership, Technical Mastery (role-specific), Collaboration, Impact, Communication. Ratings: 1–5.
- Promotion eligibility: generally requires >= 4.0 average on role competencies across two consecutive quarters plus demonstrated stretch work and leadership impact.
- Performance improvement plan (PIP): used when performance < 2.5 average despite documented coaching. PIP steps: 1) defined improvement objectives, 2) 60-day measurable plan, 3) weekly manager check-ins, 4) final assessment and HR review.

Feedback best practices for managers:
- Make feedback timely and specific; cite examples and desired change.
- Balance strengths with development; include actionable next steps.
- Document important conversations in manager notes (private) and update development plans.
- If there are performance concerns, engage people-ops early (no later than two coaching cycles).

4) Manager guide: hiring & performance hygiene checklist

Before interviewing:
- Complete interview training and unconscious bias refreshers.
- Confirm panel diversity and role-specific assessment plan.
- Prepare concrete coding/design prompts or business-case examples.

Before extending an offer:
- Confirm budget and level with People Ops and Finance.
- Collect all interviewer rubrics and ensure no category below minimum threshold without documented rationale.
- Run compensation calibration if above-band offer is proposed.

During onboarding:
- Provide clear 30/60/90 goals and check-ins.
- Assign a buddy and schedule cross-team introductions.
- Ensure access to necessary systems and permissions on day 1.

Ongoing performance hygiene:
- Hold weekly 1:1s with a shared agenda.
- Give at least two pieces of career-development feedback per quarter.
- Maintain written development plan and update quarterly.
- Escalate potential long-term concerns to people-ops early.

5) People policies (summary & links)

- Time off and PTO: standard policy summarized in 03_benefits-and-perks; managers approve within 2 business days.
- Flexible working: hybrid-first model; see remote-work guidelines for eligibility and equipment support.
- Code of conduct: all employees must sign on start; violations reported to HR and Security.
- Compensation & equity: salary bands maintained by people-ops; adjustments require approval for parity.

Quick references (contact points):

- Recruiting lead: Marco Ruiz (marco@redwood.example.com)
- IT provisioning: it-ops@redwood.example.com

Appendix: Templates and artifacts

- 30/60/90 goal template (copy to docs):
  * Objective (clear business outcome)
  * Success metrics
  * Owner & stakeholders
  * Key milestones (30/60/90)

- Interview feedback snippet (example):
  "Problem solving: 4 — Candidate demonstrated structured problem decomposition and identified tradeoffs.
  Role competence: 3 — Strong knowledge of core system, would benefit from depth in caching strategies.
  Recommendation: Hire with mentorship on system design."
